definitions.explanation: A tree that sheds its leaves annually, typically in autumn, and grows new leaves in spring.

examples.japanese: {落葉樹|らくようじゅ}は{秋|あき}に{葉|は}を{落|お}とします。
examples.english: Deciduous trees shed their leaves in autumn.

examples.japanese: {紅葉|こうよう}は{落葉樹|らくようじゅ}の{美|うつく}しさです。
examples.english: Autumn colors are the beauty of deciduous trees.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}の{落葉樹|らくようじゅ}は{葉|は}がなく{枝|えだ}だけになります。
examples.english: Deciduous trees have no leaves in winter, only branches.

notes:
{落葉樹|らくようじゅ} - trees that drop their leaves seasonally.

{落葉|らくよう} = leaf fall/shedding, {樹|じゅ} = tree

Common deciduous trees in Japan:
- {楓|かえで}・{紅葉|もみじ} (maple) - famous for autumn colors
- {銀杏|いちょう} (ginkgo) - yellow autumn leaves
- {桜|さくら} (cherry) - loses leaves after flowering
- {欅|けやき} (zelkova)

Opposite: {常緑樹|じょうりょくじゅ} (evergreen trees)

The shedding of leaves is an adaptation to survive winter by reducing water loss and protecting against cold damage.
